segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: James wrote plainly to the early church: a faith that stays only in the head is already dead.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He asked the sharp question — if a brother or sister has no clothes and no food, and you wish them well but give nothing, what good is that?

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he pointed to Abraham, who showed his faith by what he did — offering his son on the altar.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And to Rahab, who hid the spies and was counted righteous by her action, not just her words.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Belief that never moves a muscle isn't belief yet.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Real faith reaches out a hand. Let yours move — he sees every small, true thing you do.
